name: TMP36
full_name: TMP36 Low Voltage Temperature Sensor (TMP35/TMP36/TMP37 family)
description: Low-voltage analog temperature sensor with a 10 mV/C output and a 500 mV offset, so its output is 750 mV at 25 C. The 500 mV offset lets it report sub-zero temperatures from a single supply, unlike the LM35. It runs from 2.7 to 5.5 V and draws under 50 uA. Sister parts differ only in scaling: the TMP35 has no offset and the TMP37 uses 20 mV/C for higher resolution over a narrower range.

pins.name: Vout
pins.description: analog output, 10 mV/C with 500 mV offset (750 mV at 25 C)

extra.accuracy: +/-1 C typ, +/-2 C max at +25 C

typical_application: Battery-powered and low-voltage Celsius sensing into an ADC where sub-zero readings are needed on a single supply (portable instruments, environmental loggers).
gotchas: Vout has a 500 mV offset, so temperature C = (Vout_mV - 500) / 10; forgetting the offset gives a +50 C error
because of the 500 mV offset it CAN read below 0 C on a single supply (e.g. -40 C = 100 mV), unlike the LM35
TO-92 (RT-3) pin order is +Vs, Vout, GND, identical to LM35 but the transfer function differs - do not swap firmware between them
TMP35 (no offset) and TMP37 (20 mV/C) share the same package and pinout; verify the exact part marking
drive only light/known capacitive loads; large caps on Vout can cause instability
supply ripple couples into the output, so use a clean/bypassed Vs for accurate readings
